focus: Mapping no-account pairing, wait-state detection, filesystem contract, and push events into the PWA

graphEvents.label: PWA pairing, wait, filesystem, and push mapping
Device credential with nonce-bound HMAC auth

label: Pairing is a device credential: raw token is shown once, only a derived verifier is persisted server-side, and auth is a nonce-bound HMAC transcript
QR onboarding is endpoint-explicit and device-level; LAN, Tailscale, and custom modes must remain distinguishable in the PWA
Wait classification is conservative and idempotent: ANSI normalization, recent-tail focus, normalized taxonomy, prompt-hash dedupe, and meaningful-output clear
Filesystem requests have request-correlated structured responses, scope gates, jailed path validation, and retryable token-bucket rate limits
Push delivery is decoupled from the PTY stream, keyed to deduplicated waiting events, and pruned when credentials are revoked
CopyPath receives write scope and rate limiting but bypasses the destructive-operation opt-in applied to delete and rename
No privileged PWA capability is usable until the active credential has completed challenge-response and passes its required scope check
A wait notification must be idempotent for the same session, wait type, and prompt hash, while clear is driven by meaningful output or an explicit clear event
Filesystem retries must preserve request identity and distinguish retryable rate limits from terminal validation or permission errors
MobileCLI has no account system; pairing and push retention are credential-bound
The daemon broadcasts waiting state to sockets and separately sends push notifications
Delete and rename are opt-in gated, while CopyPath is not gated by the same configuration flag

direction: Treat push delivery as part of the authoritative terminal stream
reason: The daemon intentionally sends socket broadcasts and push notifications through separate paths; push failure does not represent stream failure
